title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
prompt:
Return the maximum depth of a binary tree: the number of nodes on the longest path from the root down to a leaf. An empty tree has depth 0; a single node has depth 1.

Write maxDepth(root). The helpers TreeNode, fromArray and toArray are at the top; keep them. fromArray takes LeetCode-style level order, where null means "no child here".

  • maxDepth(fromArray([3, 9, 20, null, null, 15, 7])) returns 3
  • maxDepth(fromArray([1, null, 2])) returns 2
  • maxDepth(null) returns 0

Constraints: 0 to 104 nodes. Target: O(n).

tests.name: a long chain down the left
tests.code:
const root = new TreeNode(1, new TreeNode(2, new TreeNode(3, new TreeNode(4, new TreeNode(5)))));
assertEqual(maxDepth(root), 5);

tests.name: deepest leaf is on the left, with negatives

hints: Trigger: a question about a whole tree whose answer can be built from the answers for the left and right subtrees = recursive DFS.
Base case: an empty tree (null) has depth 0. Otherwise, assume maxDepth already works for the two children (trust it), and combine.
explain:
Time O(n): every node is visited once. Space O(h) for the call stack, where h is the height: O(log n) for a balanced tree, O(n) for a chain. A BFS that counts levels gives the same answer with a queue.

Say it: "Recursive DFS. Base case null returns 0. Otherwise one plus the max of the two subtree depths. O(n) time, O(h) stack space."
